pr.title: Classify quadratic biform ranks and exclude rank 13 in the 3-by-3 block
pr.body:
This gives an effective rank formula for arbitrary quadratic biforms and a structural restriction on its two kernel indices. In particular, the nonzero fifteen-by-fifteen biform block at a=b=3 has exactly the ranks {9,12,14,15} over every field: rank13 is excluded, and universal witnesses attain the other four values.

After dividing the common coefficient gcd, let D be the largest remaining degree. The two polynomial kernel indices sum to aD, their first nonzero coefficient-kernel degree recovers both, and the full source rank is ab + min(b,mu1) + min(b,mu2). A minimum recurrence vector either has Hankel rank two and degree at least ceil((a-1)D/2), or comes from a rational root of height h and degree (a+1)h. The proof includes zero endpoints, common factors, D=0 and characteristic two.

Claims: AI-QUADRATIC-KERNEL-INDICES-001 and AI-QUADRATIC-INDEX-DICHOTOMY-002, both proof-written-unreviewed. The prior general biform kernel-bundle identity and existing special-family formulas retain their credit. External inputs: Schoemann–Wiedmann arXiv:1712.03056v1, Theorem2.1; De Teran–Dopico–Mackey MIMS EPrint2013.47 (August22 2013), Theorem6.5. Exact source versions, hypotheses and local hashes are recorded in sources.json.

Validation:
- Published verifier compares 2,010 complete source matrices over Q,F2,F3,F5, including every nonzero F2 triple for a=2,3.
- Six original focused tests,18 repository consistency tests and3 integrated top-coefficient tests pass.
- All five frozen archive replays pass; ten source files verified.
- Expanded structural controls pass locally (2,050 source comparisons and10 focused tests); their publication is pending completion of the already-running regression process so its saved input report stays stable.
- Full local regression suite and current required CI remain pending.

Reproduction: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_quadratic_kernel_indices.py -v; python -m unittest discover -s tests -v; python tools/replay.py.

This is a biform-block result, not a classification of every full cyclic-tensor slice. No source-space cap, compatible three-leg maps, degeneration, independent mathematical review, formalization or exponent improvement is claimed.

Prove all-field rank formula for biforms with one polynomial top coefficient (#217)

## New mathematical result

For any field K, a >= 2, 1 <= e < b, and f(x,z) = c_0 + ... + c_(e-1)
z^(e-1) + w(x) z^e with nonzero constant c_0, constant lower
coefficients, and nonzero deg(w)=d<a, the literal full cyclic-source
biform matrix satisfies

    rank R_(a,b)(f) = ab + sum_(j=0)^(e-1) min(b, d floor((a+j)/e)).

This holds in every characteristic, with no additional coefficient
guard. In particular, it handles the genuine three-term non-diagonal
f=1+z+(1+x^d)z^2 and all e>=2. The proof parametrizes the e free
terminal polynomial coordinates, then establishes predictable degrees
using a residue-indexed triangular leading-coefficient matrix. It
retains every original source coefficient column.

## Evidence

- 900 exhaustive GF(2) and 1,836 exhaustive GF(3) full-source rank
comparisons;
- 216 deterministic GF(5)/GF(7)/GF(101) comparisons and 420 exact degree
witnesses;
- 24 separately implemented direct-coefficient SymPy/QQ ranks;
- three focused unittests, including an off-by-one mutation control,
passed locally.

Totals: 3,372 exact modular ranks plus 24 characteristic-zero checks,
all passing. Commands, code, pinned receipt and a precise continuation
record are committed. Local environment: Python 3.13.5 / SymPy 1.14.0.
Global repository regression and historical archive replay were not
completed in this run because the isolated public-network Pyroam runner
returned an internal error; hosted current-head required CI remains
mandatory.

## Claims and dependencies

Adds AI-TOP-COEFFICIENT-BIFORM-RANK-001 with status
**proof-written-unreviewed**, independent_review=false,
improves_omega=false. Credits original literal source convention (pinned
source blob), preceding affine-z result #209 at its exact head, and
distinct #171/#186/#207 research. No unmerged runtime dependency or
external theorem is imported. Both archived 2026-10-20 research
directories are untouched.

Concurrent consolidation #214 may change STATUS, PROVENANCE and the
claim ledger on main. Reconcile the new main and rerun all required
checks before any merge; do not silently overwrite its source records.

## Limitations

The theorem classifies *individual* biform source slices with constant
lower coefficients. General u(x)+z*v(x)+z^2*w(x) minimal indices,
compatible three-leg tensor maps, auxiliary cost, and a full asymptotic
exponent implication remain open. No arithmetic exponent improvement
below 9/4 or independent mathematical review is asserted.

**Do not merge** until current-head required CI passes, all review
discussions are resolved, and the claim proof is checked against the
exact stated family.

Study full-channel paired maps through overlapping coefficient windows (#215)

## Result and scope

This PR adds `AI-PAIRED-COLUMN-OVERLAP-001`, a written, unreviewed
obstruction for paired-source maps with fixed injective
polynomial-column routing and arbitrary regular square channel matrices.
The first map and auxiliary maps may have Laurent poles, and the two
tensor contributions may cancel poles.

For target first dimension `D = lr`, covered-coordinate count `N`,
good-leading-coordinate count `G`, and overlap-component product `c`,
the auxiliary first-flattening rank is at least `max(0, D - N + G - c)`.
The formal flattening statement holds over every field; over C it also
bounds ordinary border rank. At fixed width and near-full outer
dimensions, only `o(n)` singular leading channel blocks force `n^2 -
o(n^2)` repair cost. Full channel rank is allowed.

The proof accounts separately for the ordinary leading intersection, all
new directions created by saturation, and cancellation through the
saturated auxiliary-kernel lattice. General column-mixing maps and
extensively singular leading families remain outside this obstruction.
No improved exponent is claimed.

## Evidence and dependencies

- Add the proof, source pins, standard-library exact rational verifier,
retained seven-case control report, and six package tests.
- Reconstruct native source terms and independently reconstruct
coefficient-window slices. Controls cover separated integer
restrictions, a full-channel example attaining the `D - 1`
first-flattening bound, boundary windows, actual leading rank loss,
polar cancellation, and a moving restriction that requires the
saturation correction.
- Register one new claim and update status, active-work, and provenance
summaries. Preserve all 295 existing main claim objects, existing
source/code/dependency/workflow files, and both protected research
archives.
- Both runtime source pins are on `bd03b9d`. PR211 is credited at
immutable head `1cce4e64`; its proof digest verifies, it is not a
runtime dependency, and the necessary saturated-kernel argument is
reproduced here without its earlier low-channel-rank hypothesis.

## Validation

Reviewed head: `f8fdcd314d7a0740ebc36e70e76b348b8fa33935`; exact tree:
`bd8908108844b3ea4e212204bbed15d54668d89a`.

All 27 executed tests passed: six package tests, nine repository
metadata/archive checks, and 12 baseline profile/support checks. The
retained report matches all seven native controls, covering 4,277 target
coefficient positions and 23,722 source-slice positions. The damaged
integer construction is rejected. No full regression or historical
replay was rerun for this focused review.

+# Full-channel overlap and the cost of leading rank loss
+
+October 23, 2026. Owner-directed OpenAI Codex work. Claim
+`AI-PAIRED-COLUMN-OVERLAP-001` is written and unreviewed.
+No matrix multiplication exponent improves.
+
+## 1. Result and scope
+
+The paired source is
+
+\[
+Q_{n,m}=\sum_{p,q<n}\sum_{y,v<m}
+ A_{p,q}B_{y,q+v}C_{p+y,v},\qquad n\ge1,\quad m\ge2.
+\]
+
+Its first leg has dimension `n^2`; each other leg has dimension
+`m(n+m-1)`. The target is
+
+\[
+M(l,m,r)=\sum_{i<l,j<r,\alpha<m}
+ a_{i,j}b_{j,\alpha}c_{\alpha,i},\qquad D=lr.
+\]
+
+Work over a field K, with O=K[[t]] and L=K((t)). Choose injections
+
+\[
+\sigma_B:\{0,\ldots,r-1\}\longrightarrow\{0,\ldots,n+m-2\},
+\quad
+\sigma_C:\{0,\ldots,l-1\}\longrightarrow\{0,\ldots,n+m-2\}.
+\]
+
+At retained source polynomial columns, the long maps are
+
+\[
+B_{y,\sigma_B(j)}\mapsto
+ \sum_{\alpha<m}\beta_j(t)_{y,\alpha}b_{j,\alpha},\qquad
+C_{\sigma_C(i),v}\mapsto
+ \sum_{\delta<m}\gamma_i(t)_{v,\delta}c_{\delta,i},       \tag{1}
+\]
+
+where each channel matrix belongs to Mat_m(O). Other source columns
+map to zero. The coefficients may depend arbitrarily on the retained
+column. In particular, their common shift-window span and their channel
+rank may both be full. The routing injections are fixed for the family.
+
+For a source column s define its covered first indices
+
+\[
+J(s)=\{s-m+1,\ldots,s\}\cap\{0,\ldots,n-1\}.
+\]
+
+Let U_B be the union of J(sigma_B(j)) over all retained B columns.
+Let U_B^g use only columns whose beta_j(0) is invertible. Define U_C and
+U_C^g in the same way. Put
+
+\[
+N=|U_B||U_C|,\qquad G=|U_B^g||U_C^g|.
+\]
+
+For each side, retain only its good source-column positions in the full
+window interval `[m-1,n-1]`. Join two positions when their distance is
+strictly less than m. Let c_B,c_C be the numbers of connected components,
+with zero for an empty set, and put c=c_B c_C.
+
+**Theorem.** Suppose arbitrary Laurent first maps and arbitrary Laurent
+maps on a fixed auxiliary tensor R give
+
+\[
+(A(t),B(t),C(t))Q_{n,m}+E_R(t)=M(l,m,r)+O(t).            \tag{2}
+\]
+
+The two contributions in (2) need not be regular separately. Then
+
+\[
+\boxed{\operatorname{rank} R_{A\mid BC},\ \underline R(R)
+ \ \ge\ \max(0,D-N+G-c).}                            \tag{3}
+\]
+
+The flattening statement holds over every field for the stated formal
+identity. Over C it gives the displayed usual border-rank lower bound.
+This is a restriction on the maps (1), not a lower bound for arbitrary
+paired-source constructions. Mixing distinct polynomial columns on
+either long leg is outside the theorem.
+
+## 2. The ordinary leading intersection
+
+Let H_0 be the first-slice plane of `(id,B(0),C(0))Q`. Write a first
+parameter as f=(f_pq), extending it by zero outside the source square.
+At target outer position (i,j), its m-by-m channel block is
+
+\[
+\beta_j(0)^T F_{ij}(f)\gamma_i(0),\qquad
+F_{ij}(f)_{y,v}=f_{\sigma_C(i)-y,\sigma_B(j)-v}.       \tag{4}
+\]
+
+Let T be the target first-slice plane. Its blocks are `w_ij I_m`.
+If either channel matrix in (4) is singular, equality with a target
+slice forces w_ij=0. The same conclusion holds if either window is
+outside `[m-1,n-1]`: F then has a zero row or a zero column.
+
+At a remaining good pair, both matrices are invertible, so
+
+\[
+F_{ij}(f)=w_{ij}\,\beta_j(0)^{-T}\gamma_i(0)^{-1}.
+                                                               \tag{5}
+\]
+
+Consider two good C positions separated by delta with `0<delta<m`,
+and fix one good B position. Their windows share `m-delta` full rows.
+Restricting (5) to these common source rows gives
+
+\[
+w_{ij}K=w_{i'j}K',                                      \tag{6}
+\]
+
+where K and K' are nonzero matrices. Each consists of a nonempty subset
+of rows of an invertible matrix. Thus the two scalar coordinates either
+are proportional with a fixed nonzero ratio, or both must vanish.
+The same argument for B positions uses common columns.
+
+The graph on good outer pairs is the Cartesian product of the two
+position graphs. It has c_B c_C connected components. Along each
+component, (6) leaves at most one scalar degree of freedom; a cycle may
+remove that degree of freedom. All other scalar coordinates vanish.
+Consequently
+
+\[
+\dim(H_0\cap T)\le c.                                 \tag{7}
+\]
+
+This argument needs invertibility of individual channel matrices, not
+low rank of a common channel factor. It also explains why separated
+routing components cannot be omitted from the bound.
+
+## 3. Count every direction created by a singular leading map
+
+Let H(t) be the first-slice plane of `(id,B(t),C(t))Q` over L, and
+write r_gen=dim H(t), r_0=dim H_0. Source parameters outside U_C x U_B
+have zero image for every t, hence
+
+\[
+r_{\rm gen}\le N.                                     \tag{8}
+\]
+
+At every good leading pair, (4) can be inverted to read the entire
+coefficient window of f. These windows cover U_C^g x U_B^g. A parameter
+in the leading slice-map kernel therefore vanishes on every one of its
+G coordinates, proving
+
+\[
+r_0\ge G.                                              \tag{9}
+\]
+
+Let bar(H) be the saturated limit of H(t): intersect H(t) with the
+ambient free O-module and reduce modulo t. This intersection is a
+saturated submodule over the discrete valuation ring O. A Smith basis,
+or successive elimination of lowest valuations, shows that its reduction
+has dimension r_gen. Every regular source column reduces into bar(H),
+so H_0 is contained in bar(H). Therefore
+
+\[
+\dim\bigl(\bar H/H_0\bigr)=r_{\rm gen}-r_0\le N-G.
+\]
+
+Passing from H_0 to bar(H) can enlarge its intersection with any fixed
+linear space by at most that quotient dimension. Combining with (7),
+
+\[
+\dim(\bar H\cap T)\le c+N-G.                          \tag{10}
+\]
+
+In particular, no coefficientwise limit of a raw polar source column
+has been taken. Saturation accounts for cancellations and for every
+new slice direction.
+
+## 4. Auxiliary poles cannot evade the dimension budget
+
+Let k be the first flattening rank of E_R(t) over L. It is at most the
+first flattening rank of R. Its kernel V in the D-dimensional target
+first-covector space has dimension at least D-k.
+
+The saturated lattice V intersect O^D has a reduction bar(V) of the same
+dimension. For each of its basis vectors w(t), equation (2) gives
+
+\[
+(A(t),B(t),C(t))Q(w(t))
+ =M(w(0))+O(t),                                        \tag{11}
+\]
+
+because E_R(t)(w(t)) is exactly zero over L. Each right side lies in the
+saturated source lattice. Its reduction lies in bar(H). Since M has
+injective first flattening, the independent vectors of bar(V) give at
+least D-k independent members of bar(H) intersect T. By (10),
+
+\[
+D-k\le c+N-G.
+\]
+
+This proves the flattening bound (3). A tensor of border rank q has
+first flattening rank at most q: its `(q+1)` minors vanish on rank-q
+tensors and on their closure. This supplies the border-rank conclusion.
+Ramified formal parameters may be renamed t. No bound on first-map or
+auxiliary pole orders is needed.
+
+## 5. Consequences for a scalable construction
+
+If every retained leading channel matrix is invertible, U_B^g=U_B and
+U_C^g=U_C. The lower bound is simply
+
+\[
+\underline R(R)\ge D-c_Bc_C.                          \tag{12}
+\]
+
+For contiguous full-window routing on each side, c_B=c_C=1. Thus even
+full channel rank leaves an auxiliary first-flattening cost at least
+`lr-1`. Arbitrary first-map poles do not change this conclusion.
+
+More generally, fix m and take l/n,r/n to one. Suppose all but o(n) of
+the retained leading channel matrices are invertible on each side.
+The retained injections omit o(n) source columns. A good source-column
+set of size n-o(n) covers n-o(n) first indices: the map
+`s -> min(s,n-1)` is injective except for at most m-1 upper-end positions.
+Thus G=n^2-o(n^2), while N is at most n^2.
+
+Each extra connected component among the good interior positions needs
+at least m-1 missing positions between components. Hence c_B,c_C=o(n),
+and (3) yields
+
+\[
+\underline R(R)\ge n^2-o(n^2).                        \tag{13}
+\]
+
+The construction criterion requires a subquadratic correction. A route
+within (1) must therefore use extensive leading singularity, or change
+the routing model to mix polynomial columns.
+
+There is a quantitative version, still with fixed m and l/n,r/n tending
+to one. Suppose the fractions of retained
+leading invertible blocks, divided by n, tend to alpha and beta. The
+coverage and missing-position counts above imply
+
+\[
+\liminf\frac{\underline R(R)}{n^2}
+ \ge \max\left(0,\alpha\beta-
+  \frac{(1-\alpha)(1-\beta)}{(m-1)^2}\right).           \tag{14}
+\]
+
+For equal fractions alpha=beta, a subquadratic correction requires
+`alpha<=1/m`. At width four, retaining a nonsingular leading channel
+block on more than one quarter of each long leg already forces a
+positive quadratic cost by this estimate. This is a necessary condition
+inside (1), not a claim that the remaining singular families work.
+
+## 6. Exact constructions that test the boundary
+
+### Separated windows give a genuine restriction
+
+Put k=floor(n/m), and select source polynomial positions
+`s_i=m(i+1)-1`, for i<k, on both long legs. Use identity channel maps.
+The windows are disjoint. Map a source A coordinate to a_ij exactly
+when
+
+\[
+p=mi+m-1-y,\quad q=mj+m-1-y
+\quad\text{for some }0\le y<m,
+\]
+
+and to zero otherwise. Literal substitution gives
+
+\[
+Q_{n,m}\ \ge\ M(k,m,k)                                \tag{15}
+\]
+
+over every field, with unit coefficients and no cancellation. Here
+c_Bc_C=k^2=D and (12) permits zero repair. The outer ratio is about 1/m,
+so this calibration does not supply the near-full construction criterion.
+
+### A full-channel example attains the `D-1` flattening bound
+
+Over Q, choose m distinct nonzero rationals lambda_a and let
+`V[y,a]=lambda_a^(-y)`. For full windows at positions z_i,s_j, put
+
+\[
+\beta_j^T=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_a^{-s_j})V^{-1},
+\qquad
+\gamma_i=(V^T)^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_a^{-z_i}),
+\qquad
+f_{pq}=\sum_a\lambda_a^{p+q}.
+\]
+
+Then F_ij(f)=V diag(lambda_a^(z_i+s_j)) V^T, and every mapped channel
+block is I_m. Map A_pq to f_pq a_00. The source image is
+`a_00 tensor sum_(i,j,alpha) b_(j,alpha)c_(alpha,i)`.
+Its residual to M has first-flattening kernel exactly the line of
+constant arrays w_ij, hence rank D-1. The encoded source contraction
+has full channel rank m. This example lies outside the earlier strict
+low-channel-rank hypothesis and attains (12) when the two graphs are
+connected. Sharpness here concerns the flattening bound, not an exact
+tensor border-rank formula for the residual.
+
+## 7. Evidence boundary
+
+The proof establishes the uniform statement. The accompanying exact
+controls reconstruct native source terms and compare every output
+coefficient. They test full channel rank, disconnected components,
+leading rank loss, and pole cancellation. Finite controls do not replace

+"""Exact native-source controls for the full-channel overlap theorem.
+
+Only the Python standard library is used. Complete tensor coefficients,
+including all implicit zeros, are compared. Formal maps are finite Laurent
+polynomials over Q; no floating-point decision is used.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+from fractions import Fraction as F
+import hashlib
+import itertools
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+
+
+def rank(rows):
+    """Rank of sparse rational rows without modifying the input."""
+    pivots = {}
+    for raw in rows:
+        row = {k: F(v) for k, v in raw.items() if v}
+        while row:
+            p = min(row)
+            if p not in pivots:
+                scale = row[p]
+                pivots[p] = {k: v / scale for k, v in row.items()}
+                break
+            scale = row[p]
+            for k, v in pivots[p].items():
+                value = row.get(k, F(0)) - scale * v
+                if value:
+                    row[k] = value
+                else:
+                    row.pop(k, None)
+    return len(pivots)
+
+
+def dense_rank(matrix):
+    return rank([{j: value for j, value in enumerate(row) if value}
+                 for row in matrix])
+
+
+def inverse(matrix):
+    n = len(matrix)
+    rows = [[F(v) for v in row] + [F(i == j) for j in range(n)]
+            for i, row in enumerate(matrix)]
+    for j in range(n):
+        p = next(i for i in range(j, n) if rows[i][j])
+        rows[p], rows[j] = rows[j], rows[p]
+        scale = rows[j][j]
+        rows[j] = [value / scale for value in rows[j]]
+        for i in range(n):
+            if i != j and rows[i][j]:
+                scale = rows[i][j]
+                rows[i] = [a - scale * b for a, b in zip(rows[i], rows[j])]
+    return [row[n:] for row in rows]
+
+
+def identity(m):
+    return [[F(i == j) for j in range(m)] for i in range(m)]
+
+
+def poly(value=0, degree=0):
+    return {degree: F(value)} if value else {}
+
+
+def add(left, right, scale=1):
+    out = dict(left)
+    for degree, value in right.items():
+        new = out.get(degree, F(0)) + scale * value
+        if new:
+            out[degree] = new
+        else:
+            out.pop(degree, None)
+    return out
+
+
+def mul(left, right):
+    out = {}
+    for a, x in left.items():
+        for b, y in right.items():
+            out = add(out, {a + b: x * y})
+    return out
+
+
+def evaluate(value, t):
+    return sum((coefficient * F(t) ** degree
+                for degree, coefficient in value.items()), F(0))
+
+
+def constant_blocks(matrices):
+    return [[[poly(value) for value in row] for row in matrix]
+            for matrix in matrices]
+
+
+def constant_first(values):
+    return {pq: {a: poly(value) for a, value in images.items() if value}
+            for pq, images in values.items()}
+
+
+def target(l, m, r):
+    return {(i * r + j, j * m + a, a * l + i): poly(1)
+            for i, j, a in itertools.product(range(l), range(r), range(m))}
+
+
+def native(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, first):
+    """Expand the literal n^2*m^2 source terms and all local-map entries."""
+    b_index, c_index = {s: j for j, s in enumerate(sb)}, {s: i for i, s in enumerate(sc)}
+    l = len(sc)
+    out = {}
+    expanded = 0
+    for p, q, y, v in itertools.product(range(n), range(n), range(m), range(m)):
+        j, i = b_index.get(q + v), c_index.get(p + y)
+        if j is None or i is None:
+            continue
+        for a, av in first.get((p, q), {}).items():
+            for alpha, bv in enumerate(beta[j][y]):
+                if not bv:
+                    continue
+                for delta, cv in enumerate(gamma[i][v]):
+                    if not cv:
+                        continue
+                    term = mul(mul(av, bv), cv)
+                    key = (a, j * m + alpha, delta * l + i)
+                    out[key] = add(out.get(key, {}), term)
+                    expanded += 1
+    return {key: value for key, value in out.items() if value}, expanded
+
+
+def window_slices(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, at=0):
+    """Reconstruct source slices from coefficient windows, independently of native()."""
+    l = len(sc)
+    bs = [[[evaluate(value, at) for value in row] for row in block] for block in beta]
+    cs = [[[evaluate(value, at) for value in row] for row in block] for block in gamma]
+    rows = [{} for _ in range(n * n)]
+    for i, z in enumerate(sc):
+        for j, s in enumerate(sb):
+            for y in range(m):
+                for v in range(m):
+                    p, q = z - y, s - v
+                    if not (0 <= p < n and 0 <= q < n):
+                        continue
+                    row = rows[p * n + q]
+                    for alpha in range(m):
+                        for delta in range(m):
+                            value = bs[j][y][alpha] * cs[i][v][delta]
+                            if value:
+                                key = (j * m + alpha, delta * l + i)
+                                row[key] = row.get(key, F(0)) + value
+    return [{key: value for key, value in row.items() if value} for row in rows]
+
+
+def target_rows(l, m, r):
+    return [{(j * m + a, a * l + i): F(1) for a in range(m)}
+            for i in range(l) for j in range(r)]
+
+
+def covered(n, m, positions):
+    return sorted({q for s in positions for q in range(max(0, s - m + 1), min(n, s + 1))})
+
+
+def components(n, m, positions):
+    values = sorted(s for s in positions if m - 1 <= s <= n - 1)
+    groups = []
+    for value in values:
+        if not groups or value - groups[-1][-1] >= m:
+            groups.append([])
+        groups[-1].append(value)
+    return groups
+
+
+def geometry(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma):
+    good = []
+    for positions, blocks in ((sb, beta), (sc, gamma)):
+        good.append([s for s, block in zip(positions, blocks)
+                     if dense_rank([[evaluate(value, 0) for value in row]
+                                    for row in block]) == m])
+    ub, uc = covered(n, m, sb), covered(n, m, sc)
+    gb, gc = covered(n, m, good[0]), covered(n, m, good[1])
+    cb, cc = components(n, m, good[0]), components(n, m, good[1])
+    d, nn, gg, c = len(sb) * len(sc), len(ub) * len(uc), len(gb) * len(gc), len(cb) * len(cc)
+    return {"all_covered": [ub, uc], "good_covered": [gb, gc],
+            "good_source_columns": good, "components": [cb, cc],
+            "D": d, "N": nn, "G": gg, "c": c,
+            "auxiliary_flattening_lower_bound": max(0, d - nn + gg - c)}
+
+
+def subtract_tensor(left, right):
+    out = dict(left)
+    for key, value in right.items():
+        out[key] = add(out.get(key, {}), value, -1)
+    return {key: value for key, value in out.items() if value}
+
+
+def tensor_rows(tensor, count, at):
+    rows = [{} for _ in range(count)]
+    for (a, b, c), value in tensor.items():
+        coefficient = evaluate(value, at)
+        if coefficient:
+            rows[a][(b, c)] = coefficient

+
+
+def serial_tensor(tensor):
+    return [[*key, [[degree, str(value)] for degree, value in sorted(poly_value.items())]]
+            for key, poly_value in sorted(tensor.items())]
+
+
+def digest(value):
+    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()).hexdigest()

+    if any(s < 0 or s >= n + m - 1 for s in sb + sc):

+    l, r, d = len(sc), len(sb), len(sc) * len(sb)

+
+October 23, 2026. Owner-directed Codex research. This is a written,
+unreviewed sequel to [the two-index formula](proof.md). Its checking
+belongs to the same generating session, not independent mathematical
+review or formalization. It supplies no tensor construction or improved
+matrix-multiplication exponent.
+
+The new restriction is on the possible first index. A minimum-degree
+recurrence vector either comes from a rational root of the homogeneous
+quadratic, with a precisely determined degree, or has degree in a short
+interval forced by the externally credited matrix-polynomial index sum.
+No claim is made that every integer allowed by these conditions occurs.
+
+## 1. Statement
+
+Keep the main proof's hypotheses: K is any field, a>=2, b>=3, and
+u,v,w are polynomials of degree below a, not all zero. In this note
+u,v,w always denote the primitive triple after dividing their common
+gcd. Put D=max(deg u,deg v,deg w), and let mu1<=mu2 be the indices
+proved in the main note, so
+
+    mu1+mu2=aD,       delta=mu1<=floor(aD/2).
+
+Use the homogeneous binary quadratic over K(x)
+
+    q(Z0,Z1)=u Z0^2+v Z0 Z1+w Z1^2.                       (1)
+
+A K(x)-rational root is represented by a coprime polynomial pair (s,t)
+with us^2+vst+wt^2=0. Its height is max(deg s,deg t). Such a pair is
+unique up to a nonzero constant, so its height is well defined. If one
+entry is zero, the other is a nonzero constant and the height is zero.
+Let h be the smallest rational-root height, or infinity if there is
+no rational root. Set
+
+    L=ceil((a-1)D/2),           U=floor(aD/2).
+
+**Theorem.** A polynomial recurrence vector lambda of minimum vector
+degree delta has one of the following two types:
+
+1. Its a-by-three Hankel matrix has rank two over K(x), and delta>=L.
+2. That matrix has rank one, and for some rational root [s:t] of (1),
+
+       lambda_j=c s^(a+1-j)t^j,   c in K^*,
+       delta=(a+1)max(deg s,deg t).                         (2)
+
+Consequently, with the evident infinity conventions,
+
+    min(L,(a+1)h) <= mu1 <= min(U,(a+1)h).                 (3)
+
+If q is irreducible as a homogeneous binary quadratic over K(x),
+there is no rational root and therefore
+
+    ceil((a-1)D/2) <= mu1 <= floor(aD/2).                   (4)
+
+If a rational root has minimum height h with (a+1)h<L, then the
+first index is known exactly:
+
+    mu1=(a+1)h,               mu2=aD-(a+1)h.               (5)
+
+In fact (3) also fixes mu1 at (a+1)h in the equality case
+(a+1)h=L. Every first index strictly below L must be of the root
+form (5), not merely an arbitrary small integer. These restrictions
+can eliminate candidate degrees before the exact onset test; they
+do not replace that test for the remaining interval.
+
+## 2. Minimum vectors are primitive
+
+The polynomial solution module is the kernel of
+
+    u lambda_r+v lambda_(r+1)+w lambda_(r+2)=0,
+                           0<=r<a.                       (6)
+
+A nonzero vector of minimum degree delta exists by the main proof.
+Its coordinates have gcd one up to a constant. Otherwise dividing
+all of them by a nonconstant common factor would preserve (6) and
+strictly decrease the vector degree. Rescale so the gcd is one.
+
+Let H_lambda have rows
+
+    (lambda_r,lambda_(r+1),lambda_(r+2)),  0<=r<a.          (7)
+
+It is nonzero, since every coordinate of lambda occurs in it. Its
+right kernel contains (u,v,w)^T, so its normal rank is either one
+or two. Its polynomial degree, and the grade used below, is exactly
+delta: every coordinate of lambda occurs among its entries.
+
+## 3. Rank two: explicit polynomial kernel bases
+
+Suppose H_lambda has rank two over K(x). Its right kernel is
+one-dimensional, generated by (u,v,w)^T. Primitivity of the triple
+means that a rational multiple of this vector is polynomial only
+when its multiplier is in K[x]. For example, multiply the polynomial
+coordinates by a Bezout identity for u,v,w to recover that multiplier.
+Thus its polynomial right kernel has basis (u,v,w)^T and right
+minimal index D.

+For a>=3, define a-2 row vectors q^(j), 0<=j<=a-3, by placing
+u,v,w in positions j,j+1,j+2 of a row of length a, and zero elsewhere.
+Their product with column k of H_lambda, for k=0,1,2, is
+
+    u lambda_(j+k)+v lambda_(j+k+1)+w lambda_(j+k+2)=0.

+The equation is available because 0<=j+k<=a-1. Consequently all
+q^(j) lie in the left kernel. They are independent over K(x):
+identifying a row vector with its polynomial in z, they are

+left-kernel dimension is a-2, these vectors form its complete basis
+over K(x). This proves the required basis claim directly from (6),
+without importing a scalar Hankel annihilator classification.

+They also generate the entire polynomial left kernel over K[x].

+Hankel classification from Section 5 of the main proof applies over
+this field, with no characteristic assumption. If lambda_0=0, only
+the final coordinate can be nonzero. Primitivity then makes that

+height. No separability or nonvanishing middle coefficient is
+required. This proves the rank-one branch in every characteristic.

+## 5. Consequences and caveats
+
+Every rational root of minimum height h gives a vector of degree
+(a+1)h, so mu1<=min(U,(a+1)h). A minimum vector of rank two has
+degree at least L; one of rank one has degree at least (a+1)h.
+This proves (3), including the absence of roots. The exact low-height
+conclusion (5) follows by comparing the two bounds in (3).

+The term "irreducible" in (4) refers to the homogeneous degree-two
+form (1). An affine linear polynomial u+vz may be irreducible as an
+affine polynomial while its degree-two homogenization has the root
+at infinity. In particular w=0 supplies [s:t]=[0:1], and u=0 supplies

+For D=0, the main theorem already gives mu1=mu2=0, and the present
+bounds reduce to zero. A constant irreducible quadratic can have
+no K-rational root in that case, so no root existence is inferred.

+In characteristic two an irreducible quadratic may be inseparable.
+Neither proof branch uses differentiation, distinct roots, or division
+by two; the same conclusions apply. The rank-two bound is a necessary
+condition, not a classification of all attainable splitting types.

+and 6. These are arithmetic restrictions, not assertions that each
+listed case is attained.

+# Exact ranks for biforms with one polynomial top coefficient
+
+October 23, 2026. Owner-directed AI-assisted research. Claim AI-TOP-COEFFICIENT-BIFORM-RANK-001 is proof-written-unreviewed: this file provides a written proof and finite exact controls, not an independent mathematical review, a tensor target, or an exponent improvement.
+
+## Statement and coefficient convention
+
+Let K be any field, a >= 2, b >= 2, 1 <= e < b, and m = a+b-1. Consider
+
+    f(x,z) = c_0 + c_1*z + ... + c_(e-1)*z^(e-1) + w(x)*z^e,
+
+where c_s belongs to K, c_0 is nonzero, and w(x) is a nonzero polynomial of degree d < a. The coefficients below the highest z-power are constants; only the highest coefficient may depend on x.
+
+Define the literal cyclic-source coefficient matrix with rows (j,L), 0<=j<b and 0<=L<m; columns (H,r), 0<=H<m and 0<=r<a; and entry
+
+    R[(j,L),(H,r)] = coefficient of x^(H-j)*z^(L-r) in f.
+
+Out-of-range coefficients are zero. This is the full, untruncated source matrix used in the main-branch slice-rank discussion and PR #209.
+
+**Theorem.** Put q_j = floor((a+j)/e) for 0<=j<e. Then, over every field and every permitted choice of coefficients,
+
+    rank_K R_(a,b)(f) = a*b + sum_(j=0)^(e-1) min(b, d*q_j).       (1)
+
+For d=0 the formula gives rank ab. Since sum_j q_j=a, when b>=d*ceil(a/e) the rank is exactly ab+ad. All statements hold without characteristic exceptions.
+
+For the genuinely three-term family f=1+z+(1+x^d)*z^2 with 1<=d<a and b>=3, (1) gives
+
+    rank = ab + min(b, d*floor(a/2)) + min(b, d*ceil(a/2)).
+
+For example, a=3,b=7,d=2 gives rank 27 and a=4,b=5,d=3 gives rank 30. These are neither binomial source slices nor diagonal polynomials f(xz). They do not construct compatible maps on three tensor legs.
+
+## Proof over an arbitrary field
+
+Only row groups L=0,...,a+e-1 can be nonzero, totaling (a+e)b active rows. Describe a linear dependence among those rows by polynomials
+
+    lambda_L(x) = sum_(j=0)^(b-1) lambda_(j,L)*x^j,
+    0<=L<=a+e-1,
+
+all of degree <b. Contracting against a column (H,r) reads the coefficient of x^H in
+
+    c_0*lambda_r + sum_(s=1)^(e-1) c_s*lambda_(r+s)
+                 + w(x)*lambda_(r+e).                           (2)
+
+Each expression in (2) has degree at most (a-1)+(b-1)=m-1. Because the literal matrix contains every H=0,...,m-1, the row dependence vanishes exactly when (2) vanishes as a complete polynomial identity for every r=0,...,a-1. In particular no highest-degree coefficient is dropped.
+
+The nonzero constant c_0 makes this a polynomial recurrence that can be solved backwards:
+
+    lambda_r = -(1/c_0)*(sum_(s=1)^(e-1) c_s*lambda_(r+s)
+                                + w*lambda_(r+e)),              (3)
+
+for r=a-1,...,0. Thus the e terminal polynomials lambda_a,...,lambda_(a+e-1) are freely chosen from K[x]. For j=0,...,e-1, define V_j by choosing terminal lambda_(a+j)=1 and all other terminal polynomials zero. These V_j form a free K[x]-basis of the complete polynomial solution module.
+
+Assume d>0. Each entry V_j(i) expands as a sum of paths from index i to terminal index a+j: a step of size s<e contributes the constant factor -c_s/c_0, while a step of size e contributes the polynomial factor -w/c_0. There can be at most q_j=floor((a+j)/e) size-e steps. Consequently every coordinate of V_j has degree at most delta_j=d*q_j.
+
+Write a+j=e*q_j+r_j with 0<=r_j<e. At coordinate i=r_j, the path with q_j size-e steps is the unique path attaining that number of polynomial steps: it consists entirely of size-e steps. Its leading coefficient is
+
+    (-lc(w)/c_0)^(q_j),                                    (4)
+
+which is nonzero. Every other path has fewer polynomial steps, so has degree strictly below delta_j. For every coordinate i>r_j, a path with q_j size-e steps would require a total step length at least e*q_j > a+j-i. Such a path cannot occur, so the degree-delta_j coefficient is zero. If q_j=0, the same statements hold because r_j=a+j is a free terminal coordinate, with V_j(r_j)=1 and V_j(i)=0 for all i>r_j.
+
+The residues r_j form a permutation of 0,...,e-1. Restrict the leading coefficient vector of each V_j at degree delta_j to the first e row-group coordinates. After ordering the columns by r_j, these vectors form a triangular e-by-e matrix with nonzero diagonal (4), because the entries with i>r_j vanish. Therefore the degree-delta_j leading coefficient vectors of all V_j are linearly independent over K, even in positive characteristic.
+
+For any polynomials P_j, not all zero, linear independence prevents cancellation at the largest weighted degree:
+
+    deg(sum_j P_j*V_j) = max_(j:P_j != 0)(deg(P_j)+delta_j),  (5)
+
+where degree of a polynomial vector means the maximum of its coordinate degrees. Thus all coordinates of the sum have degree <b if and only if each P_j separately satisfies deg(P_j)<b-delta_j. The active-row kernel therefore has dimension
+
+    sum_(j=0)^(e-1) max(0,b-d*q_j).                        (6)
+
+If d=0, all recurrence coefficients are constants and all V_j are constant vectors. Their terminal coordinates form the identity, so they remain independent and (5)-(6) hold with delta_j=0.
+
+Subtracting (6) from the (a+e)b active rows gives
+
+    (a+e)b - sum_j max(0,b-d*q_j)
+    = ab + sum_j min(b,d*q_j),
+
+proving (1). Write a=e*k+r, 0<=r<e. Exactly r of the q_j equal k+1 and the rest equal k; hence sum_j q_j=e*k+r=a. This proves the corollary. QED.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Independent literal-source finite-field check of the top-coefficient biform rank theorem.
+
+Uses only the Python standard library. The rank oracle builds the complete
+coefficient matrix, including its zero rows, rather than using the syzygy proof.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import itertools
+import json
+from collections import Counter
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def coefficient_matrix(a: int, b: int, e: int, c: tuple[int, ...], w: tuple[int, ...], p: int):
+    """The literal R_(a,b) rows (j,L), columns (H,r)."""
+    assert a >= 2 and b > e >= 1 and len(c) == e and len(w) == a
+    m = a + b - 1
+    M = [[0] * (a * m) for _ in range(b * m)]
+    # Build from source coefficients directly, never from the recurrence.
+    for r in range(a):
+        for j in range(b):
+            for s, coefficient in enumerate(c):
+                row = j * m + (r + s)
+                col = j * a + r  # column index is actually H*a+r; H=j.
+                M[row][col] = (M[row][col] + coefficient) % p
+            for k, coefficient in enumerate(w):
+                if coefficient:
+                    row = j * m + (r + e)
+                    col = (j + k) * a + r
+                    M[row][col] = (M[row][col] + coefficient) % p
+    return M
+
+
+def exact_rank_modp(M: list[list[int]], p: int) -> int:
+    A = [row[:] for row in M]
+    nrows = len(A)
+    ncols = len(A[0])
+    rank = 0
+    for col in range(ncols):
+        pivot = next((i for i in range(rank, nrows) if A[i][col] % p), None)
+        if pivot is None:
+            continue
+        A[rank], A[pivot] = A[pivot], A[rank]
+        inv = pow(A[rank][col] % p, -1, p)
+        A[rank][col:] = [(x * inv) % p for x in A[rank][col:]]
+        for i in range(rank + 1, nrows):
+            multiplier = A[i][col] % p
+            if multiplier:
+                A[i][col:] = [(x - multiplier * y) % p for x, y in zip(A[i][col:], A[rank][col:])]
+        rank += 1
+        if rank == nrows:
+            break
+    return rank
+
+
+def predicted_rank(a: int, b: int, e: int, w: tuple[int, ...], p: int) -> int:
+    deg = max(k for k, coeff in enumerate(w) if coeff % p)
+    return a * b + sum(min(b, deg * ((a + j) // e)) for j in range(e))
+
+
+def verify(a, b, e, c, w, p):
+    expected = predicted_rank(a, b, e, w, p)
+    got = exact_rank_modp(coefficient_matrix(a, b, e, c, w, p), p)
+    if expected != got:
+        raise AssertionError(f"R({a},{b}) e={e}, c={c}, w={w} over F_{p}: expected {expected}, got {got}")
+    return expected
+
+
+def xorshift32(x):
+    x ^= (x << 13) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    x ^= x >> 17
+    x ^= (x << 5) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    return x & 0xFFFFFFFF
+
+

+    observed = set()
+    # All lower coefficients and all nonzero top polynomials, over F_2.

+                        observed.add(got)

+    # Exhaustive F_3 controls for smaller shapes.

+        for b in range(3, 6):

+                                continue
+                            verify(a, b, e, c, w, 3)
+                            counts['GF3_exhaustive'] += 1
+    # Fixed-seed, broad rectangular spectrum; coefficients are unrestricted.
+    rng = 0xB1F0A26E
+    for p in (5, 7, 101):
+        for a in range(2, 8):
+            for e in range(2, 6):
+                for b in (e + 1, e + 3, e + 7):
+                    c = []
+                    for i in range(e):
+                        rng = xorshift32(rng)
+                        c.append((rng % (p - 1)) + 1 if i == 0 else rng % p)
+                    w = []
+                    for i in range(a):

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json

+
+def rank_by_definition(a, b, e, c, w):
+    m = a + b - 1
+    poly = {(0, s): Rational(v) for s, v in enumerate(c) if v}
+    poly.update({(i, e): Rational(v) for i, v in enumerate(w) if v})
+    rows = []
+    for j in range(b):
+        for L in range(m):

+    return Matrix(rows).rank()
+

+def expected(a,b,e,w):
+    d = len(w)-1
+    while d > 0 and w[d] == 0:

+# Full-channel overlap and the cost of leading rank loss
+
+October 23, 2026. Owner-directed OpenAI Codex work. Claim
+`AI-PAIRED-COLUMN-OVERLAP-001` is written and unreviewed.
+No matrix multiplication exponent improves.
+
+## 1. Result and scope
+
+The paired source is
+
+\[
+Q_{n,m}=\sum_{p,q<n}\sum_{y,v<m}
+ A_{p,q}B_{y,q+v}C_{p+y,v},\qquad n\ge1,\quad m\ge2.
+\]
+
+Its first leg has dimension `n^2`; each other leg has dimension
+`m(n+m-1)`. The target is
+
+\[
+M(l,m,r)=\sum_{i<l,j<r,\alpha<m}
+ a_{i,j}b_{j,\alpha}c_{\alpha,i},\qquad D=lr.
+\]
+
+Work over a field K, with O=K[[t]] and L=K((t)). Choose injections
+
+\[
+\sigma_B:\{0,\ldots,r-1\}\longrightarrow\{0,\ldots,n+m-2\},
+\quad
+\sigma_C:\{0,\ldots,l-1\}\longrightarrow\{0,\ldots,n+m-2\}.
+\]
+
+At retained source polynomial columns, the long maps are
+
+\[
+B_{y,\sigma_B(j)}\mapsto
+ \sum_{\alpha<m}\beta_j(t)_{y,\alpha}b_{j,\alpha},\qquad
+C_{\sigma_C(i),v}\mapsto
+ \sum_{\delta<m}\gamma_i(t)_{v,\delta}c_{\delta,i},       \tag{1}
+\]
+
+where each channel matrix belongs to Mat_m(O). Other source columns
+map to zero. The coefficients may depend arbitrarily on the retained
+column. In particular, their common shift-window span and their channel
+rank may both be full. The routing injections are fixed for the family.
+
+For a source column s define its covered first indices
+
+\[
+J(s)=\{s-m+1,\ldots,s\}\cap\{0,\ldots,n-1\}.
+\]
+
+Let U_B be the union of J(sigma_B(j)) over all retained B columns.
+Let U_B^g use only columns whose beta_j(0) is invertible. Define U_C and
+U_C^g in the same way. Put
+
+\[
+N=|U_B||U_C|,\qquad G=|U_B^g||U_C^g|.
+\]
+
+For each side, retain only its good source-column positions in the full
+window interval `[m-1,n-1]`. Join two positions when their distance is
+strictly less than m. Let c_B,c_C be the numbers of connected components,
+with zero for an empty set, and put c=c_B c_C.
+
+**Theorem.** Suppose arbitrary Laurent first maps and arbitrary Laurent
+maps on a fixed auxiliary tensor R give
+
+\[
+(A(t),B(t),C(t))Q_{n,m}+E_R(t)=M(l,m,r)+O(t).            \tag{2}
+\]
+
+The two contributions in (2) need not be regular separately. Then
+
+\[
+\boxed{\operatorname{rank} R_{A\mid BC},\ \underline R(R)
+ \ \ge\ \max(0,D-N+G-c).}                            \tag{3}
+\]
+
+The flattening statement holds over every field for the stated formal
+identity. Over C it gives the displayed usual border-rank lower bound.
+This is a restriction on the maps (1), not a lower bound for arbitrary
+paired-source constructions. Mixing distinct polynomial columns on
+either long leg is outside the theorem.
+
+## 2. The ordinary leading intersection
+
+Let H_0 be the first-slice plane of `(id,B(0),C(0))Q`. Write a first
+parameter as f=(f_pq), extending it by zero outside the source square.
+At target outer position (i,j), its m-by-m channel block is
+
+\[
+\beta_j(0)^T F_{ij}(f)\gamma_i(0),\qquad
+F_{ij}(f)_{y,v}=f_{\sigma_C(i)-y,\sigma_B(j)-v}.       \tag{4}
+\]
+
+Let T be the target first-slice plane. Its blocks are `w_ij I_m`.
+If either channel matrix in (4) is singular, equality with a target
+slice forces w_ij=0. The same conclusion holds if either window is
+outside `[m-1,n-1]`: F then has a zero row or a zero column.
+
+At a remaining good pair, both matrices are invertible, so
+
+\[
+F_{ij}(f)=w_{ij}\,\beta_j(0)^{-T}\gamma_i(0)^{-1}.
+                                                               \tag{5}
+\]
+
+Consider two good C positions separated by delta with `0<delta<m`,
+and fix one good B position. Their windows share `m-delta` full rows.
+Restricting (5) to these common source rows gives
+
+\[
+w_{ij}K=w_{i'j}K',                                      \tag{6}
+\]
+
+where K and K' are nonzero matrices. Each consists of a nonempty subset
+of rows of an invertible matrix. Thus the two scalar coordinates either
+are proportional with a fixed nonzero ratio, or both must vanish.
+The same argument for B positions uses common columns.
+
+The graph on good outer pairs is the Cartesian product of the two
+position graphs. It has c_B c_C connected components. Along each
+component, (6) leaves at most one scalar degree of freedom; a cycle may
+remove that degree of freedom. All other scalar coordinates vanish.
+Consequently
+
+\[
+\dim(H_0\cap T)\le c.                                 \tag{7}
+\]
+
+This argument needs invertibility of individual channel matrices, not
+low rank of a common channel factor. It also explains why separated
+routing components cannot be omitted from the bound.
+
+## 3. Count every direction created by a singular leading map
+
+Let H(t) be the first-slice plane of `(id,B(t),C(t))Q` over L, and
+write r_gen=dim H(t), r_0=dim H_0. Source parameters outside U_C x U_B
+have zero image for every t, hence
+
+\[
+r_{\rm gen}\le N.                                     \tag{8}
+\]
+
+At every good leading pair, (4) can be inverted to read the entire
+coefficient window of f. These windows cover U_C^g x U_B^g. A parameter
+in the leading slice-map kernel therefore vanishes on every one of its
+G coordinates, proving
+
+\[
+r_0\ge G.                                              \tag{9}
+\]
+
+Let bar(H) be the saturated limit of H(t): intersect H(t) with the
+ambient free O-module and reduce modulo t. This intersection is a
+saturated submodule over the discrete valuation ring O. A Smith basis,
+or successive elimination of lowest valuations, shows that its reduction
+has dimension r_gen. Every regular source column reduces into bar(H),
+so H_0 is contained in bar(H). Therefore
+
+\[
+\dim\bigl(\bar H/H_0\bigr)=r_{\rm gen}-r_0\le N-G.
+\]
+
+Passing from H_0 to bar(H) can enlarge its intersection with any fixed
+linear space by at most that quotient dimension. Combining with (7),
+
+\[
+\dim(\bar H\cap T)\le c+N-G.                          \tag{10}
+\]
+
+In particular, no coefficientwise limit of a raw polar source column
+has been taken. Saturation accounts for cancellations and for every
+new slice direction.
+
+## 4. Auxiliary poles cannot evade the dimension budget
+
+Let k be the first flattening rank of E_R(t) over L. It is at most the
+first flattening rank of R. Its kernel V in the D-dimensional target
+first-covector space has dimension at least D-k.
+
+The saturated lattice V intersect O^D has a reduction bar(V) of the same
+dimension. For each of its basis vectors w(t), equation (2) gives
+
+\[
+(A(t),B(t),C(t))Q(w(t))
+ =M(w(0))+O(t),                                        \tag{11}
+\]
+
+because E_R(t)(w(t)) is exactly zero over L. Each right side lies in the
+saturated source lattice. Its reduction lies in bar(H). Since M has
+injective first flattening, the independent vectors of bar(V) give at
+least D-k independent members of bar(H) intersect T. By (10),
+
+\[
+D-k\le c+N-G.
+\]
+
+This proves the flattening bound (3). A tensor of border rank q has
+first flattening rank at most q: its `(q+1)` minors vanish on rank-q
+tensors and on their closure. This supplies the border-rank conclusion.
+Ramified formal parameters may be renamed t. No bound on first-map or
+auxiliary pole orders is needed.
+
+## 5. Consequences for a scalable construction
+
+If every retained leading channel matrix is invertible, U_B^g=U_B and
+U_C^g=U_C. The lower bound is simply
+
+\[
+\underline R(R)\ge D-c_Bc_C.                          \tag{12}
+\]
+
+For contiguous full-window routing on each side, c_B=c_C=1. Thus even
+full channel rank leaves an auxiliary first-flattening cost at least
+`lr-1`. Arbitrary first-map poles do not change this conclusion.
+
+More generally, fix m and take l/n,r/n to one. Suppose all but o(n) of
+the retained leading channel matrices are invertible on each side.
+The retained injections omit o(n) source columns. A good source-column
+set of size n-o(n) covers n-o(n) first indices: the map
+`s -> min(s,n-1)` is injective except for at most m-1 upper-end positions.
+Thus G=n^2-o(n^2), while N is at most n^2.
+
+Each extra connected component among the good interior positions needs
+at least m-1 missing positions between components. Hence c_B,c_C=o(n),
+and (3) yields
+
+\[
+\underline R(R)\ge n^2-o(n^2).                        \tag{13}
+\]
+
+The construction criterion requires a subquadratic correction. A route
+within (1) must therefore use extensive leading singularity, or change
+the routing model to mix polynomial columns.
+
+There is a quantitative version, still with fixed m and l/n,r/n tending
+to one. Suppose the fractions of retained
+leading invertible blocks, divided by n, tend to alpha and beta. The
+coverage and missing-position counts above imply
+
+\[
+\liminf\frac{\underline R(R)}{n^2}
+ \ge \max\left(0,\alpha\beta-
+  \frac{(1-\alpha)(1-\beta)}{(m-1)^2}\right).           \tag{14}
+\]
+
+For equal fractions alpha=beta, a subquadratic correction requires
+`alpha<=1/m`. At width four, retaining a nonsingular leading channel
+block on more than one quarter of each long leg already forces a
+positive quadratic cost by this estimate. This is a necessary condition
+inside (1), not a claim that the remaining singular families work.
+
+## 6. Exact constructions that test the boundary
+
+### Separated windows give a genuine restriction
+
+Put k=floor(n/m), and select source polynomial positions
+`s_i=m(i+1)-1`, for i<k, on both long legs. Use identity channel maps.
+The windows are disjoint. Map a source A coordinate to a_ij exactly
+when
+
+\[
+p=mi+m-1-y,\quad q=mj+m-1-y
+\quad\text{for some }0\le y<m,
+\]
+
+and to zero otherwise. Literal substitution gives
+
+\[
+Q_{n,m}\ \ge\ M(k,m,k)                                \tag{15}
+\]
+
+over every field, with unit coefficients and no cancellation. Here
+c_Bc_C=k^2=D and (12) permits zero repair. The outer ratio is about 1/m,
+so this calibration does not supply the near-full construction criterion.
+
+### A full-channel example attains the `D-1` flattening bound
+
+Over Q, choose m distinct nonzero rationals lambda_a and let
+`V[y,a]=lambda_a^(-y)`. For full windows at positions z_i,s_j, put
+
+\[
+\beta_j^T=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_a^{-s_j})V^{-1},
+\qquad
+\gamma_i=(V^T)^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_a^{-z_i}),
+\qquad
+f_{pq}=\sum_a\lambda_a^{p+q}.
+\]
+
+Then F_ij(f)=V diag(lambda_a^(z_i+s_j)) V^T, and every mapped channel
+block is I_m. Map A_pq to f_pq a_00. The source image is
+`a_00 tensor sum_(i,j,alpha) b_(j,alpha)c_(alpha,i)`.
+Its residual to M has first-flattening kernel exactly the line of
+constant arrays w_ij, hence rank D-1. The encoded source contraction
+has full channel rank m. This example lies outside the earlier strict
+low-channel-rank hypothesis and attains (12) when the two graphs are
+connected. Sharpness here concerns the flattening bound, not an exact
+tensor border-rank formula for the residual.
+
+## 7. Evidence boundary
+
+The proof establishes the uniform statement. The accompanying exact
+controls reconstruct native source terms and compare every output
+coefficient. They test full channel rank, disconnected components,
+leading rank loss, and pole cancellation. Finite controls do not replace
+the argument or constitute independent mathematical review.
+
+The paired-source definition and correction criterion retain their
+original repository credit. The normalization of an auxiliary-kernel
+lattice follows the separate argument in PR211. The overlap graph,
+leading intersection bound, and resulting dimension budget are this
+continuation. The source pins and exact validation receipt are retained

+"""Exact native-source controls for the full-channel overlap theorem.
+
+Only the Python standard library is used. Complete tensor coefficients,
+including all implicit zeros, are compared. Formal maps are finite Laurent
+polynomials over Q; no floating-point decision is used.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+from fractions import Fraction as F
+import hashlib
+import itertools
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+
+
+def rank(rows):
+    """Rank of sparse rational rows without modifying the input."""
+    pivots = {}
+    for raw in rows:
+        row = {k: F(v) for k, v in raw.items() if v}
+        while row:
+            p = min(row)
+            if p not in pivots:
+                scale = row[p]
+                pivots[p] = {k: v / scale for k, v in row.items()}
+                break
+            scale = row[p]
+            for k, v in pivots[p].items():
+                value = row.get(k, F(0)) - scale * v
+                if value:
+                    row[k] = value
+                else:
+                    row.pop(k, None)
+    return len(pivots)
+
+
+def dense_rank(matrix):
+    return rank([{j: value for j, value in enumerate(row) if value}
+                 for row in matrix])
+
+
+def inverse(matrix):
+    n = len(matrix)
+    rows = [[F(v) for v in row] + [F(i == j) for j in range(n)]
+            for i, row in enumerate(matrix)]
+    for j in range(n):
+        p = next(i for i in range(j, n) if rows[i][j])
+        rows[p], rows[j] = rows[j], rows[p]
+        scale = rows[j][j]
+        rows[j] = [value / scale for value in rows[j]]
+        for i in range(n):
+            if i != j and rows[i][j]:
+                scale = rows[i][j]
+                rows[i] = [a - scale * b for a, b in zip(rows[i], rows[j])]
+    return [row[n:] for row in rows]
+
+
+def identity(m):
+    return [[F(i == j) for j in range(m)] for i in range(m)]
+
+
+def poly(value=0, degree=0):
+    return {degree: F(value)} if value else {}
+
+
+def add(left, right, scale=1):
+    out = dict(left)
+    for degree, value in right.items():
+        new = out.get(degree, F(0)) + scale * value
+        if new:
+            out[degree] = new
+        else:
+            out.pop(degree, None)
+    return out
+
+
+def mul(left, right):
+    out = {}
+    for a, x in left.items():
+        for b, y in right.items():
+            out = add(out, {a + b: x * y})
+    return out
+
+
+def evaluate(value, t):
+    return sum((coefficient * F(t) ** degree
+                for degree, coefficient in value.items()), F(0))
+
+
+def constant_blocks(matrices):
+    return [[[poly(value) for value in row] for row in matrix]
+            for matrix in matrices]
+
+
+def constant_first(values):
+    return {pq: {a: poly(value) for a, value in images.items() if value}
+            for pq, images in values.items()}
+
+
+def target(l, m, r):
+    return {(i * r + j, j * m + a, a * l + i): poly(1)
+            for i, j, a in itertools.product(range(l), range(r), range(m))}
+
+
+def native(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, first):
+    """Expand the literal n^2*m^2 source terms and all local-map entries."""
+    b_index, c_index = {s: j for j, s in enumerate(sb)}, {s: i for i, s in enumerate(sc)}
+    l = len(sc)
+    out = {}
+    expanded = 0
+    for p, q, y, v in itertools.product(range(n), range(n), range(m), range(m)):
+        j, i = b_index.get(q + v), c_index.get(p + y)
+        if j is None or i is None:
+            continue
+        for a, av in first.get((p, q), {}).items():
+            for alpha, bv in enumerate(beta[j][y]):
+                if not bv:
+                    continue
+                for delta, cv in enumerate(gamma[i][v]):
+                    if not cv:
+                        continue
+                    term = mul(mul(av, bv), cv)
+                    key = (a, j * m + alpha, delta * l + i)
+                    out[key] = add(out.get(key, {}), term)
+                    expanded += 1
+    return {key: value for key, value in out.items() if value}, expanded
+
+
+def window_slices(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, at=0):
+    """Reconstruct source slices from coefficient windows, independently of native()."""
+    l = len(sc)
+    bs = [[[evaluate(value, at) for value in row] for row in block] for block in beta]
+    cs = [[[evaluate(value, at) for value in row] for row in block] for block in gamma]
+    rows = [{} for _ in range(n * n)]
+    for i, z in enumerate(sc):
+        for j, s in enumerate(sb):
+            for y in range(m):
+                for v in range(m):
+                    p, q = z - y, s - v
+                    if not (0 <= p < n and 0 <= q < n):
+                        continue
+                    row = rows[p * n + q]
+                    for alpha in range(m):
+                        for delta in range(m):
+                            value = bs[j][y][alpha] * cs[i][v][delta]
+                            if value:
+                                key = (j * m + alpha, delta * l + i)
+                                row[key] = row.get(key, F(0)) + value
+    return [{key: value for key, value in row.items() if value} for row in rows]
+
+
+def target_rows(l, m, r):
+    return [{(j * m + a, a * l + i): F(1) for a in range(m)}
+            for i in range(l) for j in range(r)]
+
+
+def covered(n, m, positions):
+    return sorted({q for s in positions for q in range(max(0, s - m + 1), min(n, s + 1))})
+
+
+def components(n, m, positions):
+    values = sorted(s for s in positions if m - 1 <= s <= n - 1)
+    groups = []
+    for value in values:
+        if not groups or value - groups[-1][-1] >= m:
+            groups.append([])
+        groups[-1].append(value)
+    return groups
+
+
+def geometry(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma):
+    good = []
+    for positions, blocks in ((sb, beta), (sc, gamma)):
+        good.append([s for s, block in zip(positions, blocks)
+                     if dense_rank([[evaluate(value, 0) for value in row]
+                                    for row in block]) == m])
+    ub, uc = covered(n, m, sb), covered(n, m, sc)
+    gb, gc = covered(n, m, good[0]), covered(n, m, good[1])
+    cb, cc = components(n, m, good[0]), components(n, m, good[1])
+    d, nn, gg, c = len(sb) * len(sc), len(ub) * len(uc), len(gb) * len(gc), len(cb) * len(cc)
+    return {"all_covered": [ub, uc], "good_covered": [gb, gc],
+            "good_source_columns": good, "components": [cb, cc],
+            "D": d, "N": nn, "G": gg, "c": c,
+            "auxiliary_flattening_lower_bound": max(0, d - nn + gg - c)}
+
+
+def subtract_tensor(left, right):
+    out = dict(left)
+    for key, value in right.items():
+        out[key] = add(out.get(key, {}), value, -1)
+    return {key: value for key, value in out.items() if value}
+
+
+def tensor_rows(tensor, count, at):
+    rows = [{} for _ in range(count)]
+    for (a, b, c), value in tensor.items():
+        coefficient = evaluate(value, at)
+        if coefficient:
+            rows[a][(b, c)] = coefficient
+    return rows
+
+
+def serial_tensor(tensor):
+    return [[*key, [[degree, str(value)] for degree, value in sorted(poly_value.items())]]
+            for key, poly_value in sorted(tensor.items())]
+
+
+def digest(value):
+    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()).hexdigest()
+
+
+def inspect_case(name, n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, first, expected_exact=False,
+                 expected_residual_rank=None, require_poles=False):
+    if n < 1 or m < 2 or len(set(sb)) != len(sb) or len(set(sc)) != len(sc):
+        raise ValueError("Positive source sizes and injective routing are required")
+    if any(s < 0 or s >= n + m - 1 for s in sb + sc):
+        raise ValueError("Source routing column is outside the polynomial range")
+    l, r, d = len(sc), len(sb), len(sc) * len(sb)
+    source_tensor, expanded = native(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, first)
+    wanted = target(l, m, r)
+    residual = subtract_tensor(wanted, source_tensor)
+    if expected_exact and residual:
+        raise AssertionError((name, "constructed target identity failed"))
+    # Literal coefficientwise cancellation, including every negative order.
+    if residual and subtract_tensor(wanted, subtract_tensor(source_tensor, residual)) == {}:
+        raise AssertionError("The deliberately wrong residual sign passed")
+    total = subtract_tensor(source_tensor, {key: {e: -v for e, v in value.items()}
+                                           for key, value in residual.items()})
+    if total != wanted:
+        raise AssertionError((name, "complete cancellation identity failed"))
+    negative = sum(1 for value in source_tensor.values() for e in value if e < 0)
+    if require_poles and not negative:
+        raise AssertionError((name, "missing negative source coefficients"))
+    data = geometry(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma)
+    h0 = window_slices(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma)
+    h2 = window_slices(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, 2)
+    r0, r2 = rank(h0), rank(h2)
+    intersection = r0 + d - rank(h0 + target_rows(l, m, r))
+    if not (r0 >= data["G"] and r2 <= data["N"] and intersection <= data["c"]):
+        raise AssertionError((name, "dimension estimate failed", data, r0, r2, intersection))
+    native_first = constant_first({(p, q): {p * n + q: 1} for p in range(n) for q in range(n)})
+    full, _ = native(n, m, sb, sc, beta, gamma, native_first)
+    for at, reconstructed in ((0, h0), (2, h2)):
+        if tensor_rows(full, n * n, at) != reconstructed:
+            raise AssertionError((name, "native/window reconstruction disagrees", at))
+    rr = rank(tensor_rows(residual, d, 2))
+    # Evaluation supplies a certified minor over Q(t). If this is D, the
+    # rank is exactly D. Constant controls have their exact ordinary rank.
+    if rr < data["auxiliary_flattening_lower_bound"]:
+        raise AssertionError((name, "observed exact control violates the bound"))
+    if expected_residual_rank is not None and rr != expected_residual_rank:
+        raise AssertionError((name, rr, expected_residual_rank))
+    channel = [[F(0) for _ in range(m)] for _ in range(m)]
+    for (a, b, c_index), value in source_tensor.items():
+        if a == 0:
+            j, alpha = divmod(b, m)
+            delta, i = divmod(c_index, l)
+            channel[alpha][delta] += evaluate(value, 2) * F(2) ** j * F(3) ** i
+    channel_rank = dense_rank(channel)
+    return {"name": name, "n": n, "m": m, "target_shape": [l, m, r],
+            "routing_B": sb, "routing_C": sc, "geometry": data,
+            "leading_source_rank": r0, "source_rank_at_t2": r2,
+            "leading_target_intersection_dimension": intersection,
+            "residual_rank_at_t2": rr,
+            "residual_rank_is_exact_over_Qt": rr == d or not require_poles,
+            "source_terms": n * n * m * m,
+            "expanded_native_terms": expanded,
+            "target_coefficient_positions": m * m * d * d,
+            "source_slice_coefficient_positions_per_evaluation": n * n * m * m * d,
+            "source_negative_coefficients": negative,
+            "source_A0_channel_rank_at_t2_X2_Y3": channel_rank,
+            "complete_source_sha256": digest(serial_tensor(source_tensor)),
+            "complete_residual_sha256": digest(serial_tensor(residual)),
+            "exact_target": not residual}
+
+
+def separated_case(n, m):
+    k = n // m
+    positions = [m * (i + 1) - 1 for i in range(k)]
+    first = {(m * i + m - 1 - y, m * j + m - 1 - y): {i * k + j: 1}
+             for i, j, y in itertools.product(range(k), range(k), range(m))}
+    blocks = constant_blocks([identity(m) for _ in positions])
+    return inspect_case(f"separated-n{n}-m{m}", n, m, positions, positions,
+                        blocks, blocks, constant_first(first), expected_exact=True,
+                        expected_residual_rank=0)
+
+
+def vandermonde_case(n=5, m=3):
+    positions = list(range(m - 1, n))
+    lam = list(range(1, m + 1))
+    vi = inverse([[F(a) ** (-y) for a in lam] for y in range(m)])
+    beta, gamma = [], []
+    for s in positions:
+        beta.append([[vi[a][y] * F(lam[a]) ** (-s) for a in range(m)]
+                     for y in range(m)])
+        gamma.append([[vi[a][v] * F(lam[a]) ** (-s) for a in range(m)]
+                      for v in range(m)])
+    first = {(p, q): {0: sum(F(a) ** (p + q) for a in lam)}
+             for p in range(n) for q in range(n)}
+    result = inspect_case("connected-full-channel-sharp", n, m, positions, positions,

+"""Mathematical acceptance and boundary controls for column overlap."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import importlib.util
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import unittest
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+PACKAGE = ROOT / "research/ai/2026-10-23-column-overlap"
+SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("column_overlap", PACKAGE / "verify.py")
+VERIFY = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
+SPEC.loader.exec_module(VERIFY)
+
+
+class ColumnOverlapTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.report = VERIFY.run()
+        cls.cases = {value["name"]: value for value in cls.report["cases"]}
+
+    def test_complete_native_replay_matches_retained_report(self):
+        saved = json.loads((ROOT / "results/column-overlap-2026-10-23/controls.json").read_text())
+        self.assertEqual(self.report, saved)
+        self.assertEqual(self.report["case_count"], 7)
+
+    def test_full_channel_sharp_bound(self):
+        value = self.cases["connected-full-channel-sharp"]
+        self.assertEqual(value["source_A0_channel_rank_at_t2_X2_Y3"], 3)
+        self.assertEqual(value["leading_target_intersection_dimension"], 1)
+        self.assertEqual(value["residual_rank_at_t2"], 8)
+        self.assertEqual(value["geometry"]["auxiliary_flattening_lower_bound"], 8)
+
+    def test_component_count_and_saturation_are_both_necessary(self):
+        for name in ("separated-n6-m2", "separated-n8-m4"):
+            value = self.cases[name]
+            self.assertTrue(value["exact_target"])
+            self.assertEqual(value["leading_target_intersection_dimension"], value["geometry"]["c"])
+        moving = self.cases["exact-moving-target-requires-saturation-budget"]
+        self.assertTrue(moving["exact_target"])
+        self.assertGreater(moving["geometry"]["D"] - moving["geometry"]["c"], 0)
+        self.assertLess(moving["leading_source_rank"], moving["source_rank_at_t2"])
+
+    def test_boundary_rank_loss_and_separately_polar_control(self):
+        boundary = self.cases["zero-extension-boundary-columns"]
+        self.assertEqual(boundary["leading_target_intersection_dimension"], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(boundary["residual_rank_at_t2"], 12)
+        loss = self.cases["actual-leading-slice-rank-loss"]
+        self.assertEqual((loss["leading_source_rank"], loss["source_rank_at_t2"]), (8, 16))
+        polar = self.cases["singular-leading-block-with-pole-cancellation"]
+        self.assertGreater(polar["source_negative_coefficients"], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(polar["residual_rank_at_t2"], 16)
+
+    def test_damaged_integer_construction_is_rejected(self):
+        n, m, k = 4, 2, 2
+        positions = [1, 3]
+        first = {(m*i+m-1-y, m*j+m-1-y): {i*k+j: 1}
+                 for i in range(k) for j in range(k) for y in range(m)}
+        del first[(0, 0)]
+        blocks = VERIFY.constant_blocks([VERIFY.identity(m) for _ in positions])
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(AssertionError, "constructed target identity failed"):
+            VERIFY.inspect_case("damaged", n, m, positions, positions, blocks, blocks,
+                                VERIFY.constant_first(first), expected_exact=True)
